memory_update.text: VRT should remain the reference anchor for data-center power and thermal infrastructure, but its high attention level makes it less useful for the underfollowed discovery lane.
MOD is a high-priority underfollowed thermal candidate because data-center cooling appears increasingly material and separable from legacy thermal/HVAC activities.
NVT is a plausible underfollowed electrical/thermal infrastructure candidate due to data-center enclosures, power distribution, liquid cooling, and acquired switchgear/bus-system exposure.
POWL is a chokepoint-style electrical balance-of-system candidate; the key risk is lumpy project concentration rather than structural recurring data-center exposure.

Next pass should verify market caps, analyst coverage, data-center revenue mix, customer concentration, and whether backlog is AI/hyperscaler-linked versus ordinary industrial construction cyclicality.

POWL should be tracked as an underfollowed electrical-balance-of-system candidate tied to medium-voltage switchgear and behind-the-meter data-center power projects; key risk is lumpy mega-project exposure mixed with LNG and utility cycles.

MOD should be tracked as an underfollowed thermal-infrastructure candidate tied to data-center cooling, hybrid air/liquid cooling, heat-transfer systems, and hyperscale/colo demand; verify organic versus acquired growth.

NVT should be tracked as an underfollowed electrical components/enclosures/power-distribution candidate; verify how much infrastructure growth is AI data-center specific versus general electrification and utility demand.

Data-center power and thermal constraints are showing up in long-lead equipment categories such as transformers, switchgear, batteries, enclosures, rack-level power distribution, liquid cooling, and heat rejection rather than only in GPUs or networking chips.

Further Layer 1C work should search for even smaller US-listed component suppliers in busbars, copper products, heat exchangers, pumps, sensors, monitoring software, commissioning, and electrical/mechanical engineering services.
VRT remains the reference leader for AI data-center power/cooling infrastructure; use it as a benchmark, not the underfollowed discovery target.

NVT is a strong underfollowed/less-obvious liquid-cooling and enclosure/power-distribution candidate despite now sitting in a large-cap bucket; exposure is unusually direct through CDUs, manifolds, heat exchangers, PDUs, and reference architectures.

POWL is a switchgear/electrical-distribution bottleneck candidate; key uncertainty is whether data centers are a large share of Commercial & Other Industrial backlog or merely one of several electrification drivers.

BELFA is the most obscure candidate in this pass: possible rack/server power-conversion and connectivity exposure, but later layers must verify materiality, customer qualification, and segment contribution.

Need a follow-up pass for smaller electrical distributors, testing/certification labs, commissioning/engineering services, leak-detection/monitoring software, busbar/copper fabricators, and transformer-adjacent names because this pass mostly surfaced equipment/component manufacturers.
POWL should be tracked as an underfollowed electrical balance-of-system candidate; key verification is data-center backlog durability and margin profile.
MOD has moved from general thermal-management candidate to higher-priority data-center cooling candidate due to reported long-term data-center capacity agreement through 2029.
NVT is a less obvious but larger-cap electrical connection/protection candidate; Avail switchgear and bus-system assets may increase relevance to AI data-center power distribution.
AAON remains a hypothesis-stage data-center cooling candidate; exposure appears plausible but needs confirmation of BasX backlog conversion, liquid-cooling relevance, and margin normalization.
This pass found few clean USD 300M-10B US-listed pure plays; many direct liquid-cooling specialists are private or embedded inside larger industrial companies.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one high-attention reference leader and three plausible underfollowed direct-exposure names tied to AI data-center power/cooling bottlenecks. Vertiv is the reference anchor for end-to-end power and thermal infrastructure. Modine, nVent, and Powell Industries are more Serenity-aligned underfollowed candidates because they sit in industrial/HVAC/electrical categories rather than obvious AI software or semiconductor screens, yet their disclosed product exposure maps directly to cooling, enclosures, bus systems, switchgear, and packaged electrical infrastructure. This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around the physical infrastructure chokepoint created by AI data-center densification: medium-voltage switchgear, electrical distribution, enclosures, power connection systems, precision cooling, liquid cooling, heat rejection, and related services. The obvious reference lane remains Vertiv as the best-known pure-play read-through. The underfollowed lane surfaces Powell Industries, Modine Manufacturing, and nVent Electric as more specialized suppliers whose AI exposure may sit inside industrial, HVAC, or electrical-equipment labels rather than obvious AI screens. Claims are research leads only, not investment recommendations. Layer 1B expands the universe around AI data-center power and thermal balance-of-system. Vertiv is retained only as a high-attention reference anchor.
